checks: Read the entire 15-page WiE submission, including its account of existing law on page 2, the disputed paragraph and boxed recommendation on page 3, and later qualifications on pages 6 and 13.

Independently extracted the exact 34-page consultation draft and read operative Article 1 number 2 on page 4 and the explanatory memorandum on pages 19–21. Viewed the original submission page 3 and draft pages 4 and 20.

The draft requires both a special need and a duration of no more than six months. The last paragraph on page 21 expressly says the special-need requirement is also being codified and that not every rental of up to six months falls within the exception. This removes a possible ambiguity in the operative text.
strongest_alternative: The author could mean that duration becomes decisive above six months even when special need exists. That is correct and explains the valid adjacent criticism of an inflexible maximum. It does not rescue the separate broad assertion that the draft removes the particular occasion as a criterion. A distinction between a concrete occasion and an abstract special need also does not rescue the assertion that only one criterion remains, especially given the memorandum on page 21.
materiality: Minor: correcting the description removes one supporting premise, but the objection to a rigid six-month maximum and request for a rebuttable presumption or longer maximum remain available. Do not characterize the whole rental-policy argument as disproved.
direction: The incorrect description supplies an additional reason for the requested relaxation, so the narrow error favours that request.
limits: No adjudication of the appropriate maximum duration, individual rental eligibility, homelessness effects, or motive.
No later government or parliamentary draft was substituted for the consultation draft.
quote_note: No additional verbatim submission fragments recorded in this review; preserve the source quotation allowance.
